correctness.rationale: The source recurrences are scalar first-order stable EMAs. Substituting a harmonic input gives the standard transfer function \(H_\beta(\omega)=(1-\beta)/(1-\beta e^{-i\omega})\). Squaring the slow/fast ratio yields a quotient affine in \(\cos\omega\); differentiation gives \(2(\beta_3-\beta_1)(1-\beta_1\beta_3)/(1+\beta_3^2-2\beta_3\cos\omega)^2>0\) with respect to \(\cos\omega\), hence strict decrease in \(\omega\). The endpoint values and crossover formula follow algebraically. For constant or alternating gradients of fixed magnitude, bias correction makes the second moment exactly \(G^2\), so it cancels in the gain ratio. The actual verifier replays the recurrences and source-parameter periods; independent calculations reproduced the four quoted crossover periods and Nyquist gains.

final_claim: After AdEMAMix's slow-decay and slow-multiplier schedules settle at fixed \(0\le\beta_1<\beta_3<1\) and \(\alpha>0\), the slow-to-fast first-moment magnitude ratio is \(R(\omega)=\alpha|H_{\beta_3}(\omega)|/|H_{\beta_1}(\omega)|\) with \(H_\beta(\omega)=(1-\beta)/(1-\beta e^{-i\omega})\); it decreases strictly from \(\alpha\) to \(\alpha(1-\beta_3)(1+\beta_1)/((1+\beta_3)(1-\beta_1))\), giving the displayed unique crossover frequency when the endpoints straddle one, and the stated exact DC/Nyquist normalized-update gains for constant-magnitude inputs.
limitations: This is a steady-state one-coordinate linear-filter statement after schedules settle.
The crossover concerns the two numerator EMA channels, not the full adaptive update at intermediate frequency.
The exact normalized-update comparisons apply only to constant and alternating constant-magnitude inputs where the second moment is exactly controlled.
